seed_answers.q1: The manual never says which approval code to use. For a loyalty credit inside the 60-day window you have to use CR-LOY-60 and it only posts if the plan-change flag is clear. For retention offers above 40% you need RET-40-SUP which requires supervisor sign-off in the GLB-RET queue. Nobody tells you this, you learn it from the senior agents, and using the wrong code silently fails and the customer calls back.
seed_answers.q2: New hires use WVR-ROAM-24 for every roaming complaint. That code is only for lines migrated in 2024 and audit reverses it within 5 days if the toggle history shows the customer enabled roaming themselves. The right move is to check the toggle history first and use the goodwill credit code instead, which caps at 20% or 25 dollars.
seed_answers.q3: I refused a retroactive roaming waiver because the toggle history showed the customer enabled it himself. I did not use WVR-ROAM-24 and instead applied the goodwill credit under the standard code and documented it. He asked for a supervisor and I routed it through ESC-TIER3-MNL, and the supervisor upheld my decision.
seed_answers.q4: A family plan primary line moved abroad mid-cycle. The script had nothing, so I split the plan at the next cycle using the GLB-SPLIT-FAM procedure, kept the dependents on the discount, and manually adjusted 14 days of proration, 42.10 dollars. I set a follow-up under ESC-TIER3-MNL to confirm the split posted.

notes: Code sheet I keep: CR-LOY-60 loyalty, RET-40-SUP retention above 40%, WVR-ROAM-24 migration waiver only, ESC-TIER3-MNL supervisor queue, GLB-SPLIT-FAM family split.

followup_answers.f1: At day 58 or 59 I escalate to the retention desk instead of refusing, because the system backdates the plan change on day 61 and a plain refusal gets reversed anyway. My threshold is 3 days before the 60-day mark. If the customer is at day 30, I give the exact date and offer a one-time 100 peso courtesy credit so they do not call back angry.
followup_answers.f2: For the family plan split I used the remaining days in the cycle, 14 out of 30, times the primary line's daily rate, 3.01 dollars, which gave 42.10 dollars. I only do a manual split if the dependents are at least two lines, because for one dependent the family discount is smaller than the proration headache and I just move them to a single plan.
followup_answers.f3: The exception to my 60-day rule is a customer who changed plans because of our own outage credit. Those changes are flagged as system-initiated, and the loyalty credit posts anyway. I check the change reason code before refusing, roughly one in ten cases is this.
